calendar.impact: December shipper nominations close at 0700 MST. The registered December call (Light 14 percent, Heavy 9 percent) grades against the Enbridge notice that follows, with December still without a trade after eight sessions on Monday's settlements file. The industry inventory estimate for the week ending Nov 13 lands at 4:30 p.m. ET.
calendar.title: December Mainline nominations close, and the API estimate for the week ending Nov 13

calendar.impact: The inventory report for the week ending Nov 13 is the first inventory test of the surplus pricing behind Monday's 3.6 percent Brent fall, and the last dated outage in the window is scheduled to resume operations the same day.
calendar.title: EIA report for week ending Nov 13, and Irving Osprey resumption date

calendar.impact: The December WTI contract expires Friday, which puts the front differential's first trade, whenever it comes, inside the expiry week for a second straight week.
calendar.title: December WTI expiry

calendar.impact: Shareholders vote on the plan of arrangement under which Cenovus acquires Athabasca, with closing expected in December.
calendar.title: Athabasca special meeting on the Cenovus arrangement

calendar.impact: The wider group meets to set the 2027 production framework, with the IEA printing a fourth-quarter surplus and Goldman pencilling a 2.0 million barrel a day surplus for 2027.
calendar.title: OPEC+ ministerial meeting on the 2027 framework

changes.balance: Nothing in Monday's session changes a November or December barrel; the basin balance keeps tanking toward December storage of 76.24 million barrels against 80.6 million of working capacity into the nominations close, and the price test says the surplus is what the front month is paying for, on a book that had already liquidated.
changes.body: Brent Jan27 settled $92.44, down $3.40, and WTI Dec26 settled $85.72, down $2.84, on Monday (Reuters, Nov 16), and Asia extended the move to Brent $91.62 and WTI $84.89 at 0720 GMT on Tuesday (Reuters, Nov 17). The Brent to WTI spread held at $6.72 at the settle and $6.73 on the Asia print, so the move was a flat-price repricing. The factors on the board are the IEA fourth-quarter surplus of about 1.7 million barrels a day, Goldman's 2.0 million barrel a day 2027 surplus call, softer Chinese October throughput with stockpiling resuming, the prior week's all-builds inventory print, and VLCC rates down 64 percent in five weeks. The delayed CFTC report for Nov 10 positions puts the WTI managed money net long at 25,714 contracts, near a three-year low.
changes.conditional: A second straight all-builds inventory print on Wednesday would extend the surplus pricing; a measured Hormuz flow interruption, rather than another incident, is the print that reprices the strait against it.
changes.delta: Both benchmarks settled down more than 3 percent on Monday and fell further in Asia; the Brent to WTI spread held near $6.73 while the delayed WTI positioning print showed a net long of only 25,714 contracts
changes.source: Reuters, Nov 16 and 17, 2026; CFTC, released Nov 16, 2026
changes.title: Monday's fall was a flat-price repricing on the surplus calls, landed on a washed-out long
changes.vintage: Reuters settles, Nov 16, 2026, and overnight tape at 0720 GMT, Nov 17, 2026

changes.balance: The confirmed tempo keeps the strait's risk pricing live without removing a confirmed barrel; the flow gauge, not the incident count, is what converts tempo into supply, and the latest measured clearance is four days old.
changes.body: UKMTO Warning 207-26 records the outbound tanker struck by an unknown projectile at 0558 UTC on Nov 16, engine room fire, crew accounted for, identified by Vanguard Tech as the Panama-flagged On Phoenix. UKMTO Warning 208-26 then carried a third-party report late on Nov 16 of an attack about 7 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, crew safe and damage unknown. India's shipping minister said the LPG tanker Tara Gas was attacked on Nov 16 with all crew safe, without citing a warning number, so the link to either advisory is unconfirmed. Iranian claims through Monday ran to as many as six tankers catching fire plus a claimed supertanker sinking, with no vessel named for the sinking and no independent confirmation. Kpler's latest measured clearance, to Nov 11, is 8,264 kb/d, 48 percent of the pre-war 17,148 kb/d.
changes.conditional: A fresh measured clearance print materially below 8,264 kb/d, or confirmation of the claimed sinking by an owner, insurer, tracker or UKMTO product, converts the tempo into a supply event; continued incidents at the current measured clearance keep the surplus in charge of the front month.
changes.delta: A third UKMTO incident in three days (Warning 208-26, north of Khasab, late Nov 16), against Iranian claims of up to six tankers and a sinking that remain unconfirmed
changes.source: UKMTO via Riviera Maritime Media and Gulf Business, Nov 16 to 17, 2026; Kpler briefing, Nov 13, 2026
changes.title: Three confirmed incidents in three days, and the sinking claim still has no hull

changes.balance: December WCS remains a mark into the close that sets its apportionment; the traded deferred tightening says the winter strip is wide but not widening, and the notice that follows the close is the next physical print on the front.
changes.body: December WCS settled -$28.22 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 16) on zero lots, an eighth straight session without a December trade, with December outright at $57.50 on Monday's WTI settle. The traded strip tightened modestly on volume: Jan27 -$25.75 on 720 lots, Feb27 -$24.50 on 245 lots and Mar27 -$23.40 on 295 lots, and Houston's January ARV to TMW spread printed +$7.45 with both legs traded. November apportionment stands at Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert. December nominations close Tuesday Nov 17 at 0700 MST and the registered December call is Light 14 percent and Heavy 9 percent.
changes.conditional: A December notice at or above the registered call, or a first December trade materially wider than -$28.22, reopens the widening path; a lighter notice with the deferred tightening held extends the snap-back that began in the physical market last week.
changes.delta: December WCS marked -$28.22 on zero lots for an eighth straight session while the traded deferred strip tightened on volume, into the Nov 17 nominations close
changes.source: ICE Report Center EOD, Nov 16, 2026; Enbridge notice, Oct 20, 2026
changes.title: The front month is still a mark, and the traded strip behind it tightened

flags.body: November Mainline apportionment (Light 19 percent at Kerrobert, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert) is in effect. The registered December call is Light 14 percent and Heavy 9 percent. The evidence pack includes the balance build with supply running about 200 kb/d a month above the proven 4,541.6 kb/d egress bound into tanks, a December front month that has not traded in eight sessions on Monday's file, deferred strip tightening on volume, and a Brent to WTI spread holding near $6.73. December nominations close Tuesday Nov 17 at 0700 MST; the Enbridge notice follows and grades the call.
flags.title: December apportionment: the registered call is Light 14 and Heavy 9, nominations close Nov 17
flags.trigger: The Enbridge December apportionment notice, or a material change in the physical backdrop before the close

flags.body: Three tanker incidents are confirmed or officially reported in three days: the VLCC Al Dhannah on Nov 15, the outbound vessel in Warning 207-26 on Nov 16, and the attack reported north of Khasab in Warning 208-26 late on Nov 16, all with crews safe. Iranian claims of up to six tankers and a supertanker sinking carry no named vessel for the sinking and no confirmation. Kpler's latest measured clearance is 8,264 kb/d to Nov 11, 48 percent of pre-war. A confirmed sinking or a measured flow interruption reprices the strait; continued incidents at the current measured clearance keep the surplus in charge.
flags.title: Confirmed tanker tempo is rising while the sinking claim stays unconfirmed
flags.trigger: A confirmed hull for the claimed sinking from an owner, insurer, tracker or UKMTO product, or a fresh measured clearance print materially below 8,264 kb/d

flags.body: The delayed CFTC report for Nov 10 positions puts the NYMEX WTI managed money net long at 25,714 contracts, near the bottom of its three-year range, and the ICE Brent book stands at +133,813 after two straight cuts totalling 111,644 contracts. Saxo puts the combined net long at 202,000 contracts, a four-month low, on long liquidation. Monday's fall of more than 3 percent in both benchmarks landed after that washout, so the book has less long left to flush and no crowded long to squeeze.
flags.title: Positioning was washed out before Monday's fall: WTI net long 25,714, Brent cut by 111,644 in two weeks
flags.trigger: The next CFTC and ICE Brent commitments reports, or a flat-price reversal on a confirmed flow print
